summary: Say the counting numbers in order from 1 all the way to 30.
Count up to 10 objects, touching or pointing to each one once while saying one number.
Count up to 10 things and tell that the last number said is how many there are.
See how many are in a small group of up to 6 things at a glance, without counting.
Know and name the written numbers from 0 to 10.
Show how many a number from 0 to 10 stands for, with dots, counters or a matching group.
Begin to see that a number up to 10 can be made from two parts in different ways, like 5 as 4 and 1 or 3 and 2.
Compare two groups of up to 10 things and say which has more, which has fewer, or that they're the same.
Show putting groups together to make up to 5 with objects, pictures or a told story, and count them all.
Show taking some away from a group of up to 5 with objects, pictures or a told story, and say how many are left.
Name and describe circles, squares, triangles and rectangles, and name at least one solid shape, like a ball or a can.
Make shapes from materials, like two triangles put together to make a square.
Use position words like on, under, beside, between, in front of, behind, near and far.
Know a shape is still the same shape whatever its size and however it's turned.
Compare the heights or lengths of people and things, with words like taller, shorter and longer.
Compare containers to tell which holds more and which holds less.
Compare the weights of things, with words like heavy, light, heavier and lighter.
Talk about time within the day with words like morning, after snack and before we go home.
Sort things into groups of the same kind and say how the groups are alike and different.
Collect answers or objects and show them in a simple graph, like a picture or floor graph.
Spot, copy, continue and make repeating patterns, like red, blue, red, blue.
